extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers and policymakers interested in wartime mobilization and labor and economic stabilization policy
extracted.subtask_description: A newspaper report describing Presidential orders creating the Office of War Mobilization and a Committee on Fair Employment Practice, including the duties, powers, and policy rationales set out in those orders. Targets description and explanation of wartime administrative and anti-discrimination measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop unified programs and establish policies for maximum use of resources
rubrics_metrics.description: “To develop unified programs and to establish policies for the maximum use of the nation’s natural and industrial resources for military and civilian needs, for the effective use of the national manpower not in the armed forces, for the maintenance and stabilization of the civilian economy, and for the adjustment of such economy to war needs and conditions.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates that the Office of War Mobilization create integrated programs and policies covering resource allocation, manpower not in the armed forces, civilian economic stability, and adjustment of the civilian economy to wartime requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unify federal agency activities related to production and logistics
rubrics_metrics.description: “To unify the activities of Federal agencies and departments engaged in or concerned with production, procurement, distribution or transportation of military or civilian supplies, materials and products and to resolve and determine controversies between such agencies or departments.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives the office authority to coordinate and reconcile conflicting actions among agencies involved in production, procurement, distribution and transportation for military and civilian supply chains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to issue directives to federal agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: “To issue such directives on policy or operations to the Federal agencies and departments as may be necessary to carry out the programs developed, the policies established and the decisions made under this order.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directives issued under this authority are to be executed by all such agencies and departments, which must also make progress reports to the Office of War Mobilization as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of agencies to execute directives and report progress
rubrics_metrics.description: “It shall be the duty of all such agencies and departments to execute these directives and to make to the Office of War Mobilization such progress reports as may be required.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies are obligated to implement policies/directives from the Office and to provide progress updates; intended to ensure accountability and coordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility for director to delegate and determine manner of operations
rubrics_metrics.description: “The Office of War Mobilization may perform the functions, exercise the powers, authority and discretion conferred on it by this order through such officials and such agencies and in such manner as the director, subject to the provisions of this order, may determine.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits the director to use officials/agencies and choose operational methods, hire necessary personnel, and make provision for supplies, facilities and services within available funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment/supersession of conflicting prior executive orders
rubrics_metrics.description: “All prior Executive Orders in so far as they are in conflict herewith are amended accordingly.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes that this order takes precedence over inconsistent prior executive orders to avoid legal/administrative conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep wartime coordinating committee purposely small for effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee is to be “purposely kept small so that it can function most effectively.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational guidance that small, focused membership is preferred to ensure efficiency and effective decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include department and agency heads on committee when issues concern them
rubrics_metrics.description: “The heads of the various departments and agencies will be asked to sit with the committee whenever matters of special concern to their consideration.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides for ad hoc participation by relevant agency heads on issues of special concern to ensure input and coordination without permanently expanding committee size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational goals: streamline, avoid duplication, eliminate friction, decide quickly
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee will “streamline our activities, avoid duplication and overlapping, eliminate interdepartmental friction, make decisions with dispatch and keep both our military machine and our essential civilian economy running in team and at high speed.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets performance standards and operational priorities for wartime administration: efficiency, rapid decision-making, interagency cooperation, and synchronized military/civilian operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include anti-discrimination provision in all U.S. government contracts and subcontracts
rubrics_metrics.description: “All contracting agencies of the government of the United States shall include in all contracts hereafter negotiated or re-negotiated by them a provision obligating the contractor not to discriminate against any employee or applicant for employment because of race, creed, color, or national origin, and requiring him to include a similar provision in all subcontracts.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A binding contractual requirement imposed on government contractors and flowed down to subcontractors to prohibit employment discrimination on specified protected grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assure non-discrimination in vocational and training programs for war production
rubrics_metrics.description: “All departments and agencies of the government of the United States concerned with vocational and training programs for war production shall take all measures appropriate to assure that such programs are administered without discrimination because of race, creed, color, or national origin.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires proactive steps to ensure training and vocational opportunities tied to war production are accessible without discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish Committee on Fair Employment Practice to formulate policies and recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: “There is hereby established in the Office for Emergency Management ... a Committee on Fair Employment Practice ... The committee shall formulate policies to achieve the purposes of this order and shall make recommendations to the various Federal departments and agencies and to the President which it deems necessary.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates a central body tasked with policy development and recommendations to federal entities and the President to effect non-discrimination and full utilization of manpower.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee to recommend measures to War Manpower Commission for full utilization and training without discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: “The committee shall also recommend to the chairman of the War Manpower Commission appropriate measures for bringing about the full utilization and training of manpower in and for war production without discrimination because of race, creed, color, or national origin.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies an interagency role: advising manpower authorities on steps needed to ensure equitable utilization and training for war production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee investigative and hearing powers over discrimination complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: “The committee shall receive and investigate complaints of discrimination forbidden by this order. It may conduct hearings, make findings of fact, and take appropriate steps to obtain elimination of such discrimination.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants the committee authority to investigate, hold hearings, determine facts, and take remedial steps to eliminate discriminatory practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer of jurisdiction and records from old Fair Employment Practice committee
rubrics_metrics.description: “Upon the appointment of the committee and the designation of its chairman, the Fair Employment Practice Committee, established by executive order No. 8802 ... shall cease to exist. All records and property of the old committee ... shall be transferred to the committee. The committee shall assume jurisdiction over all complaints and matters pending before the old committee.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consolidates and continues prior work by abolishing the old committee and transferring its records, funds, and pending matters to the new committee for continuity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to appoint personnel and utilize interagency and voluntary services
rubrics_metrics.description: “Within the limits of the funds which may be made available for that purpose, the chairman shall appoint and fix the compensation of such personnel ... The committee may utilize the services and facilities of other Federal departments and agencies and such voluntary and uncompensated services as may from time to time be needed.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorizes staffing and resource arrangements including interagency cooperation and voluntary assistance subject to available funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee rulemaking power
rubrics_metrics.description: “The committee shall have the power to promulgate such rules and regulations as may be appropriate or necessary to carry out the provisions of this order.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enables the committee to issue rules/regulations to implement the anti-discrimination order effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supersede inconsistent executive orders
rubrics_metrics.description: “The provisions of any other pertinent executive order inconsistent with this order are hereby superseded.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes legal primacy of this order over earlier executive orders that conflict with its anti-discrimination requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy: maximum employment and full participation regardless of race, creed, color, or national origin
rubrics_metrics.description: “Whereas the successful prosecution of the war demands the maximum employment of all available workers regardless of race, creed, color, or national origin ... Whereas it is the policy of the United States to encourage full participation in the war effort by all persons in the United States regardless of race, creed, color or national origin ...”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the normative rationale for the Committee and contract/subcontract provisions: mobilize all available labor and ensure democratic unity by eliminating employment discrimination during the war effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of all employers and labor organizations to eliminate discrimination in employment and union membership
rubrics_metrics.description: The President declared it “the duty of all employers, including the several Federal departments and agencies and labor organizations ... to eliminate discrimination by such employers ... in hiring, tenure, terms or conditions of employment, or union membership because of race, creed, color or national origin.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directs employers (including federal entities) and labor organizations to proactively end discriminatory practices in hiring, employment conditions, tenure and union membership.
